standingRules.breadth: universe size x observation frequency x independence; event rows are not presumed independent
standingRules.cost: dual estimator plus holding-period capital turnover; exact zero means below estimator resolution
standingRules.identity: fail closed on ticker reuse, succession, delisting, outcome conditioning, and unknown known-at timestamps

formalResearchRecommendation: No candidate is approved for preregistration. One observable candidate is COST_SENSITIVE; the other leading mechanisms need bounded data audits.
nextResearchQuestions: Do not spend infrastructure capacity on ex-dividend execution modeling unless consolidated NBBO/TAQ becomes available; the one-venue IEX sanity check failed.
The bounded PIT S&P 400/600 source audit is insufficient on breadth; revisit only with an identity-safe, exhaustive family ledger covering at least 10.3 years.
ProShares exposes historical NAV/shares/AUM, but leveraged-ETF reset-flow magnitude remains blocked until derivative exposure and an independent sponsor cross-check are established.

candidates.name: Ex-dividend tax/clientele pressure
candidates.mechanism: Investors with different tax and income mandates may transact around ex-dates for non-price-maximizing reasons.
candidates.persistence_reason: Tax and mandate differences persist, but published evidence disputes how much is tax versus microstructure.
candidates.expected_distortion: Temporary price pressure around the ex-date
candidates.observability_notes: 2025 Sharadar check: 6,743 eligible domestic-common-stock dividend rows, 1,704 securities, 248 dates. No returns inspected.
candidates.reason: Breadth clears conservatively at one independent date-cluster per trading day, but a 20-day holding assumption gives 2.80% CS cost while AR reads below resolution.
candidates.independence_notes: 6,743 nominal events collapse to at most 248 date clusters; sector/issuer dependence would reduce this further.

candidates.name: Index addition / forced buying
candidates.mechanism: Benchmark additions force index trackers to buy.
candidates.persistence_reason: Tracking-error limits make the trade non-discretionary.
candidates.observability_notes: Existing S&P 500 action ledger is PIT-enumerable.
candidates.reason: Breadth MDA is 5.87%/yr; cost is below MDA but not enough to cure detectability.
candidates.independence_notes: Two rho variants reported (0.0, 0.5 standard); at positions=1 rho only affects screen_design's own internal calibration anchor, not this design's bet count (pinned behavior, see tests/test_engine/test_index_deletion_screen.py).

candidates.name: Spinoff shares dumped by ineligible holders
candidates.mechanism: Parent holders receive a security their mandate may not permit.
candidates.persistence_reason: Distribution is mechanical and the child may initially lack a natural holder base.
candidates.trigger: Dated spinoff action naming the child security
candidates.observability_notes: Market-wide actions enumerate parent and child, subject to normal identity audit.
candidates.reason: MDA 6.50%/yr is above the target despite acceptable measured costs.
candidates.independence_notes: Two rho variants reported (0.0, 0.5 standard), same positions=1 caveat as index addition.

candidates.name: S&P 500+400+600 additions, deletions, and migrations
candidates.mechanism: Index-family migration forces offsetting benchmark trades in liquid names.
candidates.expected_distortion: Temporary demand imbalance across index tracker groups
candidates.observability_notes: S&P 500 side exists; 400/600 historical change ledgers do not.
candidates.reason: The 500-only proxy is marginal (4.16% MDA); the actual family population cannot be enumerated.
candidates.missing_data_scope: Acquire or construct PIT S&P 400 and 600 change ledgers; no strategy engine work is needed.

candidates.name: IPO lockup-expiration selling pressure
candidates.mechanism: Insiders and pre-IPO holders are contractually barred from selling until a prospectus-specific release date.
candidates.persistence_reason: Contract terms are binding, though waivers and durations vary.
candidates.expected_distortion: Supply increase when locked shares become saleable
candidates.observability_notes: SEC says terms vary and directs users to each prospectus; a 180-day approximation is not identity-safe enough.
candidates.reason: Exact terms and early waivers require filing-level extraction before events can be counted.
candidates.missing_data_scope: Parse a bounded sample of 424B4/S-1 prospectuses and 8-K waivers before deciding whether market-wide extraction is justified.

candidates.name: Leveraged-ETF daily rebalance pressure
candidates.mechanism: Daily-target leveraged and inverse funds must reset derivative exposure each day.
candidates.persistence_reason: Daily target and fund flows determine required exposure independent of expected next-day return.
candidates.trigger: Daily underlying move combined with fund NAV and leverage
candidates.observability_notes: The daily mandate is public, but the repository lacks historical AUM/shares and derivative exposure needed to size flow.
candidates.reason: Mechanism is hard and frequent, but trigger magnitude is not reconstructible with current holdings data.
candidates.missing_data_scope: Test whether sponsor NAV/share files provide stable daily history for 3-5 major funds; do not build a broad ETF crawler first.

candidates.name: Reg SHO Rule 201 short-sale restriction pressure
candidates.mechanism: A 10% decline activates a price test restricting short-sale execution for the rest of the day and next day.
candidates.persistence_reason: The rule is mandatory and trigger-based.
candidates.expected_distortion: Temporary imbalance in short-sale supply and execution priority
candidates.observability_notes: Daily OHLC can suggest triggers but cannot establish exact trigger time or executable price-test state.
candidates.reason: Fail closed until official historical SSR flags or consolidated intraday trigger data are available.
candidates.missing_data_scope: Audit exchange/FINRA historical SSR lists; NYSE public halt-style history is only one year, so long-history coverage is uncertain.
candidates.missing_data_effort: SMALL discovery audit; potentially LARGE acquisition

candidates.name: Lagged 13F crowded-exit pressure
candidates.mechanism: Fund outflows or mandate changes can force managers holding the same liquid names to sell.
candidates.persistence_reason: Agency and flow constraints recur, but the contemporaneous flow is not public.
candidates.trigger: Publicly known lagged crowding plus an independently observed fund-flow shock
candidates.observability_notes: 13F holdings become public up to 45 days after quarter end; current repository has no PIT fund-flow source.
candidates.reason: Using quarter-end holdings before filing acceptance would be lookahead; crowding alone does not identify a forced sale.
candidates.missing_data_scope: A 13F ingestion path is bounded, but a PIT fund-flow source is a separate unresolved dependency.

candidates.name: Odd-lot tender provisions
candidates.mechanism: Tender terms can privilege sub-100-share holders.
candidates.persistence_reason: The provision is part of filed tender terms.
candidates.observability_notes: No structured historical event population exists in the repository.
candidates.reason: Population count and PIT terms are not yet measurable.
candidates.missing_data_scope: A bounded SEC Schedule TO search/parser plus manual term validation on a sample.

candidates.name: Distressed / post-reorg equity
candidates.mechanism: Mandates and operational frictions delay ownership of newly issued post-reorg equity.
candidates.constraint: Distress, ratings, seasoning, and benchmark eligibility
candidates.persistence_reason: Security eligibility changes more slowly than legal emergence.
candidates.observability_notes: CIK verifies a known link but no field discovers successors market-wide.
candidates.reason: The prior breadth and cost passes cannot be carried forward to a discoverable population.
candidates.independence_notes: Two rho variants reported (0.0, 0.5 standard), same positions=1 caveat.
candidates.missing_data_scope: Build a market-wide CIK/date-proximity candidate index, then independently validate every proposed old/new security link.

candidates.name: Small merger arb below institutional minimum deal size
candidates.mechanism: Large arbitrage funds cannot deploy meaningful dollars in small deals.
candidates.persistence_reason: Capacity remains uneconomic for large funds.
candidates.observability_notes: A usable cash-deal/date filter was established, but it sharply reduced the population.
candidates.reason: Honest eligibility filtering raised MDA to 4.10%/yr, above the fixed target.
candidates.independence_notes: Three variants: rho=0.0, rho=0.5 (project standard), and rho=0.2 (sensitivity only, reflecting the conventional view that merger-arb completion risk is largely deal-specific rather than market-correlated) -- reported separately, never substituted for the standard case.

candidates.name: Tax-loss selling reversal (December)
candidates.mechanism: Taxable investors realize losses near year-end.
candidates.observability_notes: Signal is constructible, but positions cluster in the same macro drawdown.
candidates.reason: Effective breadth is annual and highly correlated; MDA is 8.15%/yr.
candidates.independence_notes: Two variants: rho=0.5 (project standard) and rho=0.7 (sensitivity, reflecting measured extreme year-to-year clustering -- loser rate ranged 1.6% to 46.0% across just 4 sampled years, i.e. most 'losers' in a given year are largely the same macro bet).

candidates.name: Index deletion / forced selling
candidates.mechanism: Benchmark removals force index trackers to sell.
candidates.persistence_reason: Trackers are judged on tracking error, not execution alpha.
candidates.observability_notes: Existing S&P 500 action ledger is PIT-enumerable.

candidates.name: S&P 500 equal-weight quarterly reset pressure
candidates.mechanism: Equal-weight trackers must reset every constituent toward 0.2% each quarter.
candidates.persistence_reason: Tracking-error mandate requires the reset even when flows are predictable.
candidates.expected_distortion: Common close-auction demand tied to weight drift
candidates.observability_notes: Trigger and member population are constructible; actual dollars require AUM but are not needed to reject breadth.
candidates.reason: Roughly 2,000 security rows are only four common rule/batch events; MDA is far above 4%.
candidates.independence_notes: All constituent trades share four rebalance batches and one underlying rule; nominal rows are not independent bets.

candidates.name: Fed stress-test capital-distribution constraint
candidates.mechanism: Stress-capital requirements constrain dividends and repurchases at large banks.
candidates.observability_notes: Official annual publications identify participants and results.
candidates.reason: Many bank rows share one annual supervisory event and macro scenario; MDA is roughly 40%/yr.
candidates.independence_notes: Treat the annual release as one macro/regulatory batch, not 22 independent bank events.

candidates.name: Sub-$5 stocks excluded by fund charters
candidates.mechanism: Some fund policies prohibit very low-priced shares.
candidates.reason: Both estimators put annual cost far above MDA.
candidates.independence_notes: rho=0.5 (project standard) only -- see approximation caveats below before trusting this number.

candidates.name: Sub-$300M cap cross-sectional anomalies (momentum)
candidates.mechanism: Known momentum premium in a capacity-constrained universe.
candidates.persistence_reason: Large funds cannot efficiently hold the smallest names.
candidates.trigger: PIT market cap plus lagged momentum rank
candidates.observability_notes: Sharadar can construct the population fail-closed.
candidates.reason: Both spread estimators imply annual cost above MDA.
candidates.independence_notes: Two variants: rho=0.5 (project standard, but see note) and rho=0.15 (sensitivity -- 0.5 was calibrated on a 5-name mega-cap anchor and is not obviously the right assumption for a ~2000-name small/micro-cap cross-section, where idiosyncratic risk is proportionally much larger; reported as a range, not resolved).
